curriculum.scope_note: Particles-strand basics: distinguish elements, compounds, mixtures and pure substances, and recognise state symbols in chemical equations.
curriculum.learning_objective: Classify a substance as an element, compound, mixture or pure substance and assign appropriate state symbols in a chemical equation.

curriculum.scope_note: Particle arrangement, movement and energy in states of matter and interconversions; state-symbol vocabulary is retained under Basics.
curriculum.learning_objective: Explain a change of state by relating the named process to particle arrangement, movement and energy.

curriculum.scope_note: Diffusion and dilution explained with the particle model.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use particle movement to explain observations from gas diffusion and dilution of a coloured solution.

curriculum.scope_note: Solution formation, solubility and solubility-curve work; the practical point is retained with the content it develops.
curriculum.learning_objective: Define solution terms and use solubility data or a curve to determine how much solid dissolves at a stated temperature.

curriculum.scope_note: Physical separation methods, including chromatographic interpretation; substance classification is assigned to Basics (1.1).
curriculum.learning_objective: Select and describe a suitable separation method, then use a chromatogram or Rf value to identify mixture components.

curriculum.scope_note: Atom and molecule terminology, subatomic structure and nuclear-number vocabulary.
curriculum.learning_objective: Identify subatomic particles and use atomic number, mass number and isotope notation to describe an atom.

curriculum.scope_note: Relative atomic mass as an isotope-abundance calculation.
curriculum.learning_objective: Calculate the relative atomic mass of an element from isotope masses and abundances.

curriculum.scope_note: Periodic-table organisation, electronic configuration and broad main-group trends.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use an element’s periodic-table position to state its classification, electron configuration and likely group-related behaviour.

curriculum.scope_note: Group 1 observations, trends, prediction and electronic explanation.
curriculum.learning_objective: Predict and explain the change in Group 1 reactivity down the group using observations and outer-electron configurations.

curriculum.scope_note: Group 7 physical trends and displacement evidence, with the electronic explanation.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use halogen properties and displacement results to order Group 7 reactivity and explain the trend electronically.

curriculum.scope_note: Formation, charges, formulae and electron-transfer representation of ions and ionic compounds.
curriculum.learning_objective: Construct an ionic formula or dot-and-cross diagram from ion charges and explain the attraction between the resulting ions.

curriculum.scope_note: Core covalent-bond model and dot-and-cross representations for specified molecules.
curriculum.learning_objective: Draw a correct dot-and-cross diagram for a specified molecule and identify each shared pair as a covalent bond.

name: Formulae
include: Construct neutral ionic compound formula from named ions or supplied charges
Explain lowest ionic ratio using charge balance
exclude: Recall or infer ion charges alone
Empirical or molecular formula from composition
teaching_band_note: 5-6 monatomic; 7-8 polyatomic. Never replace source empirical band.

name: Equations
include: Add or interpret assessed state symbols
Translate supplied named reactants and products or paragraph to formula equation
exclude: Use supplied equation for moles, redox, energy or equilibrium reasoning without assessed equation construction
teaching_band_note: Activity bands are pedagogical; source empirical bands remain unchanged.

curriculum.scope_note: Identification tests for the specified gases.
curriculum.learning_objective: Choose and describe the positive test and observation for hydrogen, oxygen, carbon dioxide, ammonia or chlorine.

curriculum.scope_note: Flame tests and sodium-hydroxide tests for the specified cations.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use a flame-test colour or hydroxide-test observation to identify a specified cation and state the required reagent.

curriculum.scope_note: Wet tests for halide, sulfate and carbonate anions.
curriculum.learning_objective: Plan the specified anion tests and use their observations to distinguish chloride, bromide, iodide, sulfate and carbonate.

curriculum.scope_note: Combined qualitative-analysis pathways, including gas, ion and water tests.
curriculum.learning_objective: Combine appropriate qualitative tests to identify the ions, gases or water status represented by an unknown sample.

curriculum.scope_note: Particle-collision explanation of rate factors and catalysts.
curriculum.learning_objective: Explain how a changed rate factor or catalyst alters successful collisions or activation energy.

curriculum.scope_note: Rate graphs and reaction-profile interpretation.
curriculum.learning_objective: Interpret a rate or reaction-profile graph to compare reaction progress, activation energy or the effect of a catalyst.

specification_refs: Experimental skills: safe methods; variables; observations and measurements; data analysis; reliability
curriculum.scope_note: Rate investigations mapped to their specified practical contexts and the crosscutting experimental skills section.
curriculum.learning_objective: Plan or evaluate a rate investigation by identifying variables, controlling conditions and collecting data suitable for a conclusion.

curriculum.scope_note: Simple molecular structures, intermolecular attractions, physical properties and conductivity.
curriculum.learning_objective: Relate simple molecular structure and intermolecular attraction to melting or boiling behaviour and electrical conductivity.

curriculum.scope_note: Giant covalent structures and the property consequences of diamond, graphite and C60.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use the bonding and structure of a giant covalent substance to explain its hardness, melting point or electrical conductivity.

curriculum.scope_note: Ionic lattice properties and the conditions required for electrical conduction.
curriculum.learning_objective: Explain the melting behaviour and electrical conductivity of an ionic compound from its lattice and ion mobility.

curriculum.scope_note: Metallic lattice model and the conductivity and malleability of metals.
curriculum.learning_objective: Draw or interpret a metallic-lattice model and use it to explain a metal’s conductivity or malleability.

curriculum.scope_note: Comparative structure-property reasoning across ionic, simple molecular, giant covalent, metallic and covalent substances.
curriculum.learning_objective: Compare two structures and justify differences in melting point, conductivity or mechanical behaviour using bonding and particle models.

curriculum.scope_note: Relative formula mass, amount of substance, reacting mass and percentage-yield calculations.
curriculum.learning_objective: Calculate a chemical amount, reacting mass or percentage yield from balanced equations and supplied data.

curriculum.scope_note: Experimental formula determination and empirical-to-molecular formula calculations.
curriculum.learning_objective: Determine an empirical or molecular formula from experimental composition data and explain the required ratio calculation.

curriculum.scope_note: Solution amount, volume and concentration calculations in the context of titration.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use concentration, volume and stoichiometry to calculate an unknown amount or concentration in solution.

curriculum.scope_note: Gas-volume and molar-volume calculations at room temperature and pressure.
curriculum.learning_objective: Convert between gas amount and volume using the stated molar volume at room temperature and pressure.

curriculum.scope_note: Stoichiometric reaction equations and quantitative use of balanced equations.
curriculum.learning_objective: Write or use a balanced equation, including state symbols where required, to solve a reaction-quantity problem.

curriculum.scope_note: Acid, base and alkali definitions and neutralisation relationships.
curriculum.learning_objective: Classify a substance as an acid, base or alkali and explain neutralisation using hydrogen-ion or proton-transfer ideas.

curriculum.scope_note: Indicators and pH classification, including universal-indicator estimates.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use an indicator result or pH value to classify an aqueous solution and select a suitable indicator.

curriculum.scope_note: Acid reactions with metals, bases and carbonates, and the proton-transfer interpretation.
curriculum.learning_objective: Predict the products and write a balanced equation for a specified acid reaction with a metal, base or carbonate.

curriculum.scope_note: Solubility rules for common ionic compounds.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use the specified solubility rules to predict whether an ionic compound is soluble or forms a precipitate.

curriculum.scope_note: Preparation of pure, dry soluble and insoluble salts, including the named practicals.
curriculum.learning_objective: Select and sequence the separation, washing and drying steps needed to prepare a pure, dry sample of a specified salt.

curriculum.scope_note: Organic representation, nomenclature, homologous-series language, isomerism and reaction classes.
curriculum.learning_objective: Represent and name a specified organic compound, identify its series or reaction class, and draw valid structural alternatives where applicable.

curriculum.scope_note: Alkane formulae, saturation, structures, names and mono-substitution with halogens.
curriculum.learning_objective: Name or draw an alkane and predict the products of its specified mono-substitution reaction with a halogen under ultraviolet radiation.

curriculum.scope_note: Alkene structure, formulae, naming, bromine addition and the bromine-water test.
curriculum.learning_objective: Identify an alkene from its structure or test result and represent its reaction with bromine.

curriculum.scope_note: Crude oil as a hydrocarbon mixture, fractional distillation, fractions, fuels and combustion pollutants.
curriculum.learning_objective: Explain how fractional distillation separates crude oil and relate fraction properties or combustion products to their uses and impacts.

curriculum.scope_note: Catalytic cracking and its industrial purpose.
curriculum.learning_objective: Describe catalytic cracking conditions and explain why it changes the supply of useful hydrocarbon fractions.

curriculum.scope_note: Exothermic and endothermic changes and energy-level diagrams.
curriculum.learning_objective: Classify a reaction as exothermic or endothermic and draw or interpret its energy-level diagram.

specification_refs: Experimental skills: safe methods; observations and measurements; variables; data analysis; reliability
curriculum.scope_note: Practical energetics investigations mapped to calorimetry contexts and the crosscutting experimental skills section.
curriculum.learning_objective: Describe or evaluate a temperature-change investigation with suitable controls, measurements and evidence-based conclusions.

curriculum.scope_note: Calorimetry methods and Q = mcΔT or molar-enthalpy calculations.
curriculum.learning_objective: Calculate heat energy or molar enthalpy from a measured temperature change and supplied mass, specific heat or amount data.

curriculum.scope_note: Bond-energy model and reaction enthalpy from bond energies.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use mean bond energies to calculate a reaction enthalpy and assign the signs of bond-breaking and bond-making terms.

curriculum.scope_note: Composition of dry air and experimental determination of oxygen percentage.
curriculum.learning_objective: State the approximate composition of dry air and calculate the oxygen percentage from an appropriate experiment.

curriculum.scope_note: Oxides from combustion and decomposition, including atmospheric and acid-rain consequences.
curriculum.learning_objective: Predict or explain the formation and environmental effect of a specified oxide from its source reaction.

curriculum.scope_note: Combustion of elements and hydrocarbons, complete or incomplete products and carbon monoxide toxicity.
curriculum.learning_objective: Write or interpret a combustion equation and explain how oxygen supply changes products and hazards.

curriculum.scope_note: Carbon dioxide formation, greenhouse-gas context and identification test.
curriculum.learning_objective: Explain one specified source or environmental effect of carbon dioxide and identify it using the limewater test.

curriculum.scope_note: Hydrogen combustion, hydrogen identification and physical or chemical tests for water.
curriculum.learning_objective: Identify hydrogen or water using the specified test and relate hydrogen combustion to water formation.

curriculum.scope_note: Reversible-reaction notation and examples.
curriculum.learning_objective: Recognise a reversible reaction, use the equilibrium arrow correctly and describe a specified reversible example.

curriculum.scope_note: Dynamic equilibrium in a sealed system and the role of a catalyst.
curriculum.learning_objective: Describe the conditions and observable characteristics of dynamic equilibrium and explain why a catalyst does not change its position.

curriculum.scope_note: Temperature and pressure effects on equilibrium position.
curriculum.learning_objective: Predict the equilibrium shift caused by a temperature or pressure change and justify it from energy or gas-mole changes.

curriculum.scope_note: Reactivity-series evidence from acid, water and displacement reactions, including the specified practical.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use reaction observations to place metals in the reactivity series and predict a displacement outcome.

curriculum.scope_note: Oxidation, reduction and redox language linked to electron-transfer half-equations.
curriculum.learning_objective: Identify oxidation and reduction in a reaction and write an appropriate ionic half-equation where required.

curriculum.scope_note: Rusting conditions and prevention by barrier, galvanising or sacrificial methods.
curriculum.learning_objective: State the conditions required for rusting and explain how a named prevention method limits the process.

curriculum.scope_note: Electrolyte conductivity, electrode products, half-equations and the electrolysis practical; extraction is included where electrolysis is the method.
curriculum.learning_objective: Predict electrolysis products and write the electrode half-equations for a specified molten or aqueous electrolyte.

curriculum.scope_note: Alcohol functional group, naming, oxidation and ethanol manufacture by hydration or fermentation.
curriculum.learning_objective: Draw and name a specified alcohol, then describe one oxidation or manufacturing route with its conditions.

curriculum.scope_note: Carboxylic-acid structure, naming, reactions and the composition of vinegar.
curriculum.learning_objective: Draw or name a specified carboxylic acid and predict its reaction with a metal or metal carbonate.

curriculum.scope_note: Ester functional group, formation, representation, properties and preparation practical.
curriculum.learning_objective: Use the reactant names or formulae to draw an ester and state its formation conditions or characteristic use.

curriculum.scope_note: Addition and condensation polymers, repeat units, monomers, disposal and biodegradability.
curriculum.learning_objective: Draw or deduce a polymer repeat unit or monomer and explain one specified environmental issue of polymer disposal.

specification_refs: Experimental skills: safe and skilful practical techniques; observations and measurements
curriculum.scope_note: Practical techniques crosscutting the specified investigations; this is an atlas skill hierarchy rather than a new specification topic.
curriculum.learning_objective: Select and describe safe apparatus and measurement techniques appropriate to a specified chemistry investigation.

specification_refs: Experimental skills: devise and plan investigations; select techniques; independent, dependent and control variables
curriculum.scope_note: Planning and variable control across the specified practical contexts; no invented practical-point code is used.
curriculum.learning_objective: Plan an investigation by stating a testable relationship, identifying variables and selecting a suitable method and control strategy.

specification_refs: Experimental skills: make observations and measurements with appropriate precision; record methodically
curriculum.scope_note: Observation and measurement reporting across the specified practical contexts.
curriculum.learning_objective: Record qualitative observations and quantitative measurements with appropriate precision and units in a clear results table.

specification_refs: Experimental skills: analyse and interpret data; communicate findings with calculations and graphs
curriculum.scope_note: Data handling and representation linked to the specification’s calculations, curves, graphs and practical evidence.
curriculum.learning_objective: Process supplied or measured chemistry data using an appropriate calculation, graph or table and state a conclusion supported by it.

specification_refs: Experimental skills: draw evidence-consistent conclusions; assess reliability; evaluate accuracy and validity
curriculum.scope_note: Evaluation, reliability and improvement across the specified practical contexts; this does not claim a full specification-coverage audit.
curriculum.learning_objective: Evaluate the reliability and validity of an investigation, identify a material limitation and propose a justified improvement.
